ledger.note: 4 February 1923: Mosul is left out of the Lausanne talks. 'The parties decided that the Mosul Question would be excluded from the Lausanne Treaty negotiations' (4 February 1923) and referred to the League of Nations; Britain had occupied Mosul on 10 November 1918. A diplomatic dispute, not a campaign: Britain had held the vilayet since 10 November 1918.

region.text: the vilayet of Mosul, occupied by the British on 10 November 1918 (Ninawa, Kirkuk, Erbil, Dohuk and Sulaymaniyah)

ledger.note: 1926: Turkey accepts the League's award of Mosul. The League 'made a decision on December 16, 1925, allotting the vilayet of Mosul to Iraq'; 'Turkey reluctantly assented to the decision by signing the Frontier Treaty of 1926', and Iraq agreed to give Turkey 10 percent of the royalties of the Turkish Petroleum Company concession. The page gives no month for the treaty.

3 October 1932: Iraq becomes independent. 'The treaty came into force on 3 October 1932'; 'The role of the United Kingdom in the formal administration of the Kingdom of Iraq was ended in 1932' and Iraq joined the League of Nations the same day. The state and its shape continue; colour continues. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): type occupation_end with kingdom-of-great-britain (was rename, though the name did not change): the group scope draws the British and French mandates as occupations. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain (ended 1800) -> british-colonial-empire, which records the same occupation (fx-44 handoff)]

ledger.note: May 1941: Britain defeats the Iraqi rising and occupies Iraq. The war ran 2-31 May 1941 (infobox 'Allied victory'), the 20th Indian Brigade having landed unopposed at Basra on 18 April; an armistice was signed on 31 May and 'The British decided not to occupy Baghdad immediately'. Infobox 'British occupation of Iraq until 1947'. The extent of the occupation is the page's 'Iraq'; the kingdom stayed in being. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain (ended 1800) -> british-colonial-empire, which records the same occupation (fx-44 handoff)]

14 July 1958: the monarchy is overthrown. Infobox 'Monarchy abolished: 14 July 1958'; the army coup of the 14 July Revolution under Abd al-Karim Qasim deposed Faisal II. The Arab Federation formed with Jordan on 14 February 1958 was dissolved on 2 August 1958 by the new Iraqi government (Arab Federation page).

wars.name: Mosul Question

zones.text: the vilayet of Mosul, occupied by the British on 10 November 1918 (Ninawa, Kirkuk, Erbil, Dohuk and Sulaymaniyah)

wars.outcome: Mosul was left out of the Lausanne settlement (4 February 1923), the League of Nations allotted the vilayet to Iraq on 16 December 1925 and Turkey assented in the Frontier Treaty of 1926 for 10 percent of the oil royalties.
wars.note: No fighting: the page records the Istanbul Conference (19 May 1924) and the League dispute only.

wars.name: Anglo-Iraqi War
wars.outcome: British victory in four weeks (2-31 May 1941); the rebellion was suppressed and Britain occupied Iraq until 1947. No border changed.

wars.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War (Iraqi expeditionary force)

zones.text: the strategic triangle in Samaria bounded by the Arab towns Nablus, Jenin and Tulkarm

wars.outcome: An Iraqi brigade group crossed the Jordan on 15 May 1948, besieged Gesher, was repulsed and moved into the Samaria triangle (Nablus, Jenin, Tulkarm), where it became stationary; no Iraqi territory changed.
wars.note: Page read to 100,000 characters; the Iraqi withdrawal of 1949 is not on the part read. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): zone added: the Iraqi force 'moved into the strategic triangle in Samaria bounded by the Arab towns Nablus, Jenin and Tulkarm' (1948 war page) and 'withdrew its forces from the region in March 1949' (1949 Armistice Agreements page); the hold is not yet a ledger occupation.

certainty.note: The Mosul vilayet frontier with Turkey was disputed until 1926; the desert frontiers were undefined.

The Turkish frontier follows the Frontier Treaty of 1926 and the Saudi frontier and neutral zone the Uqair protocol of 2 December 1922; the desert frontiers with Transjordan and Syria are approximate, and the Iranian and Kuwaiti frontiers were not read.

notes: Start and end differ from Cliopatria (1932-1957): the page founds the kingdom on 23 August 1921 under the mandate and ends it on 14 July 1958. 1921-1931 and 1943-1946 and 1958 are new keyframes on the 1932/1947/1956 outlines. The British mandate of 1920-1932 and the occupation of 1941-1947 are the British dossiers' to draw as occupations (this ledger records the same events from Iraq's side, 1941-1947 as an occupation by kingdom-of-great-britain; the mandate itself is not a ledger event here). Overlap with other dossiers: Cliopatria's Arab Federation row (1958-1959, 537,952 km2) covers Iraq in 1958; the arab-federation dossier and this one both claim the land from 14 February to 14 July 1958, and iraqi-republic should take it from July 1958 although Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic starts in 1960. The Arab Federation is a union of two kingdoms that kept their domestic government, so no merge event is recorded. Not reached within the five-page budget: the Iraqi revolt of 1920 and the 1930 treaty, the Shatt al-Arab treaty with Iran (1937), the frontier with Kuwait and Transjordan, the 1936 and 1941 coups. Cliopatria's Saudi-Iraq neutral zone is excluded from both shapes until the 1982 partition, so the 1922 loss is recorded with the counterpart nobody. The neutral zone region is built from Cliopatria differences, not a name; the gazetteer lacks 'Saudi-Iraqi Neutral Zone' (hint: kite-shaped, about 28-30 N, 44.5-46.5 E). Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): the mandate of 1921-1932 is now an occupation pair with kingdom-of-great-britain (replacing the rename of 3 October 1932); the 1948 war has the Samaria triangle as its zone.
